 ....
( SHRI SARANJIT SINGH CHAWLA ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENT NO.2)

This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e cour  following:
 ORDER

This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short MV Act) against the impugned award dated 16.1.2018 passed by the 3rd Addl. Member, MACT, Neemuch (M.P.) in claim case No. 27/2016 for enhancement of the compensation amount.

2 The relevant and necessary facts of the case are that on 1.8.2013 at about 7 pm when appellant/claimant was starting his vehicle at that time driver of offending motorcycle bearing Kamal Ahir vs Milap Kothari on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159678654/
1 registration No. MP-44-ME-8001 driven the vehicle at high speed rashly and negligently and hit the appellant due to which appellant sustained grievous injuries on his right leg, he got fractured and admitted in Deepak Orthopedic Hospital and thereafter he was referred to Porwal Hospital Bhilwada.
The incident was reported at police station Neemuch.
Accordingly offence has been registered against respondent no. 1.

At the time of incident the vehicle was insured with respondent no.2.
3

The appellant/claimant has preferred claim petition before the below tribunal and tribunal after scrutinizing the evidence available on record awarded the compensation amount of Rs. 86,197/-
with interest @ 9% per annum in favour of appellant/claimant.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, the appellant has preferred this appeal.

4 Learned counsel for appellant submits that compensation awarded by below tribunal is very less and on the lower side under various heads, the below tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the heads of loss of income, pain and suffering, loss of future income and deficiency in work capacity, the appellant is income tax payee therefore, his income was assessed on very lower side.
Hence, he prays that the impugned award be modified and the compensation amount be enhanced appropriately.
5 None for respondent no.1 though duly served.
6 Learned counsel for respondent No. 2 opposed the prayer by submitting that impugned award passed by the below tribunal is just and proper and does not deserve for any interference.
7 Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record with due care.

8 From perusal of the impugned award it appears that the appellant/claimant Kamal (PW-1)
examined himself before the below tribunal.

His statement is well supported by statement of Dr. J.P.
Joshi (PW-2).
Respondent no. 2 has examined Narendra Kumar Manager Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. before the below tribunal.
The claimant has also proved documents (Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-87) during his evidence which includes the FIR (Ex.P-4), charge sheet (Ex.P-3) and other documents of criminal prosecution.

Therefore, on the basis of aforesaid oral as well as documentary evidence, it is proved that incident took place by offending vehicle which was driven by respondent no. 1 and offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 2 insurance company.
There is no evidence available on record to establish that there was any breach of insurance policy by owner or driver of the offending vehicle.
9 The moot question to be addressed in this appeal preferred by the appellant is, as to whether the tribunal was justified in awarding the compensation of Rs. 86,197/- to the appellant.

10 The below tribunal on the basis of the statements of appellant Kamal and Dr. J.P. Joshi has proved that appellant/claimant sustained 15% permanent disability, the tribunal has awarded Rs.
27,197/- towards medical expenses, the permanent disability sustained by appellant is not in the nature which was continuous and prolong, therefore, the below tribunal has rightly declined any Kamal Ahir vs Milap Kothari on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159678654/
2 amount for future treatment.

11 So far as the compensation under other heads is concerned, the tribunal has granted Rs. 5,000/-
under the head of pain and suffering; Rs.
5,000/- for transportation charges; Rs. 9,000/- for attender; Rs. 10,000/- for special diet and Rs.
30,000/- for permanent disability.
Thus, the claim tribunal has awarded total sum of Rs. 86,197/- as compensation to appellant which is based upon evidence available on record.
Therefore, the aforesaid finding given by the below tribunal appears to be just, proper and adequate.
Hence appellant is not deserve for any enhancement.
12 In the result, this appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
Both the parties shall bear their own cost.
(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Kamal Ahir vs Milap Kothari on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159678654/
